chapter: Joe Oliver, Tom Brown and closing
title: Tom Brown and Steve Brown
summary: He recalls Tom Brown's temper and style and praises Steve Brown on bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: One thing I plan to ask you, if there's anything you can tell us about Tom Brown, since we never got to talk to him, or any of our Tulane tapes. I know you played with him, recorded with him a lot. Any remarks about him?

Yeah, well, Tom Brown, uh, was a very interesting person to watch. He was different from anybody, and he could, uh, he could analyze what you were talking about immediately, and he had a hair, uh, trigger temper, you know? Yeah. If he didn't like it, boy, you were gonna get it right away. That's right. And, uh, he was very different from Steve. Steve Brown, who I think is the greatest white bass player I've ever heard in my life. Oh, just out of the world, that marvelous bass player. Too bad those kind of people, those kind of white rhythm people can't stay in the audience here. Yeah. But we have to have piccolo players on bass fiddle here, you know?

Uh, well, anyway, uh, Tom, uh, had a hair-trigger temper, and he just didn't take anything from anybody. But he, he was a, he was a cute guy to be with. Yeah.
